subject: POC kickoff: orchestration flow, load-window tradeoffs & guest pass details
messages:
From: Sabrina Cole <sabrina@voltis-retail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: devops@voltis-retail.com
Date: 2026-07-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Voltis POC kickoff — preferred dates and onsite/virtual question

Hi Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Voltis is keen to kick off the hands-on POC where we can run prompt walkthroughs, routing checks and a short load test. 2-hour working session + 1-hour prep sounds good to us.

A couple of asks from our side before we lock a date:
- Can Redwood provide a recommended load-test window (concurrent sessions / tokens) we should expect so our infra lead can reserve network quota?
- We have a preference for onsite (NYC) so our retail ops folks can attend, but we also need streaming/recording permissions documented in case some folks join remotely.

Preferred kickoff dates: July 15–20 (any morning ET). If any date in that range won't work for you, let us know alternatives.

Sabrina
Sabrina Cole
Head of Product, Voltis Retail
Sabrina.Cole@voltis-retail.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sabrina Cole <sabrina@voltis-retail.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Voltis POC kickoff — preferred dates and onsite/virtual question

Hi Sabrina — great to hear. July 15–20 works; we have an open slot on July 16 from 10:00–13:00 ET that fits a 2h hands-on + 1h prep cadence. If that’s acceptable we’ll reserve the team and the room.

Quick answers to your asks:
- Recommended load-test target: for a first pass we suggest a stepped test that peaks at ~25 concurrent interactive sessions and 10k tokens/min overall. That gives us visibility into batching behavior and routing decisions without stressing production infra. We’ll provide a short JSON test plan.
- Onsite logistics: we can support onsite in NYC. We’ll need a visitor list 48 hours before arrival for building security, and we can record the session if you sign the attached recording consent (see site-access-form.pdf). Remote folks can join via a streaming link; Redwood will enable screen share + participant chat.

Attached: draft POC runbook & site access form.

Action items:
1) Confirm July 16 10:00–13:00 ET (Marcus to send invite + meeting room reservation).
2) Voltis to send visitor names and any special access notes by July 14.
3) Voltis devops to review load target and confirm bandwidth.

Thanks — I’ll pencil the slot and follow up with a calendar invite that includes the runbook and test plan.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
From: devops@voltis-retail.com
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-05T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Voltis POC kickoff — preferred dates and onsite/virtual question

Marcus / Naomi,

We’ll aim for the recommended load profile but have a couple of constraints: our retail edge team has a 9–11 AM maintenance window on July 16 that reduces available throughput. Is it possible to shift the load test to the later hour (11:30–12:30 ET) within your 10:00–13:00 slot? That would let us run the necessary backend spikes without hitting maintenance.

Also, do you have a preferred CDN/ingress measurement hook for token accounting? We can provide a temporary test endpoint.

Thanks,
Voltis DevOps
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: devops@voltis-retail.com, Sabrina Cole <sabrina@voltis-retail.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-05T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Voltis POC kickoff — timing + test hooks

Thanks for the heads up. Shifting the active load window to 11:30–12:30 ET is fine — we’ll structure the session as:
- 10:00–10:30 ET: introductions & prompt walkthroughs (routing and prompt templates)
- 10:30–11:30 ET: hands-on prompt tuning and routing checks (no high-volume load)
- 11:30–12:30 ET: stepped load test (target peak ~25 concurrent, 10k tokens/min)
- 12:30–13:00 ET: wrap, next steps, and immediate notes

For measurement hooks: we can instrument token accounting from our side if Voltis provides a test ingress (preferred) — otherwise we’ll report observed concurrency and token throughput from the Redwood side. Please send the temporary endpoint and any auth creds to naomi@redwood.com.

I’ll update the runbook with the final timing and include an AV checklist for the NYC room (projector input, laptop adapters, streaming firewall ports).

—Marcus
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Sabrina Cole <sabrina@voltis-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-06T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final details: visitor list, recording consent, and AV dry run

Sabrina — quick checklist to close out before we send the calendar invite: please reply to this email with the following by EOD July 14 so building security and our ops team can complete prep:

- Full names + government ID type for all onsite visitors (for badge pre-clear).
- Which attendees require screen-share permission vs presenter-only (we will lock recording to presenters by default).
- Any restricted data types we should avoid sending to the demo environment (we’ll scrub prompts and use synthetic examples if needed).

Operational notes:
- Recording: we can record the session; recording consent is attached. If you prefer no recording, indicate that and we’ll disable recording but still stream to remote attendees.
- AV dry run: we offer a 20-min remote AV dry run the day before (July 15) at 16:00 ET. It covers projector handshake, firewall ports, and streaming link verification. Strongly recommended.

I’ll attach the updated runbook with the final 10:00–13:00 ET breakdown and the load test JSON plan once we receive your endpoint.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
